etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin radiatio, radiationis. By surface analysis, radiate +‎ -ion.

definitions.definition: The shooting forth of anything from a point or surface, like diverging rays of light.
The process of radiating waves or particles.
The transfer of energy via radiation.

quote.citation: 1986, "Weird Al" Yankovic (lyrics and music), “Christmas at Ground Zero”, in Polka Party!‎[1]:
quote.text: It's Christmas at ground zero / And if the radiation level's OK / I'll go out with you / To see all the new / Mutations on New Year's Day

definitions.definition: (evolutionary theory, countable) A rapid diversification of an ancestral species into many new forms.

quote.citation: 2014, Elizabeth Kolbert, chapter 8, in The Sixth Extinction: An Unnatural History, Henry Holt and Company:
quote.text: So the question is: have plants and animals retained over this huge amount of time—whole radiations of mammals have come and gone in this period—have they retained these potentially costly characteristics?

quote.citation: 2016, Donald R. Prothero, The Princeton Field Guide to Prehistoric Mammals, page 136:
quote.text: The second [canid group] is the radiation of dogs in South America that began when the first canids arrived about 3 Ma, after crossing the Panama land bridge (Fig. 5.4).
